catalyst_sustain_demo.name: Catalyst Sustain Demo
catalyst_sustain_demo.description: Demonstrates the catalyst bracelet's sustain affordance — hold a state while time runs. A glowing torus floats above a pedestal; a trail of after-images shows the integral of held-position over time. First place the player meets 'hold this while time passes.'

slope_tangent_demo.name: Slope Tangent Demo
slope_tangent_demo.description: A sine curve with a moving point that drags its tangent line. Where the curve is steep, the tangent tilts; at zero crossings, it flattens. The first map showing rate as a thing alongside the thing — derivative as instantaneous slope.

integral_area.name: Integral Area
integral_area.description: Area under a curve as accumulation, animated. A sweep marker progresses left to right; vertical strips light up as they enter the swept region. The definite integral made visible: the headline accumulation artifact for the change sequence.

derivative_pair.name: Derivative Pair
derivative_pair.description: Two stacked curves with a shared vertical sweep line. f on top, f' below. Shows the derivative as a function in its own right.

velocity_arrow.name: Velocity Arrow
velocity_arrow.description: A puck moves around a closed track with an arrow riding on it. Length = speed, direction = motion. Velocity as the visible derivative of position.

partial_derivative_terrain.name: Partial Derivative Terrain
partial_derivative_terrain.description: A wavy terrain. Two arrows ride a moving sample point, one for partial-x, one for partial-y. First map showing two-axis differentiation.

riemann_pump.name: Riemann Pump
riemann_pump.description: Three side-by-side strip displays of the same curve, accumulated via left, right, and midpoint sums. The strip count pumps up and down, showing convergence and bias.

dna.default: field=cells, coding=magnitude - cells is the `_:` branch of the match, which is the shipped stream function v=(dPsi/dz, -dPsi/dx) with Psi=sin(kx+t)cos(kz+t) and k=2.5, unchanged line for line; magnitude is the `_:` branch of the tint, the shipped arrow_color->arrow_color_hot lerp on |v|/3.5. Neither branch is reachable unless a map names a value, and apply_grid_config ignores any word not in FIELDS/CODINGS, so a typo falls back to the shipped look rather than blanking the field. Nothing rebuilds: both are read fresh every frame by _update_arrows, so the 35 cells across seven maps (Flow_Field, Flow_Particle_Pulse, VFM_Field, Trial_rooms_change, Trial_gate8_cha_size, Trial_gate8_cha_type, Zone_TemporalStorage) build and animate exactly as before.
dna.was: one field and one colour rule, both hard-coded in the body of _field_vector and _update_arrows. grid_cols/grid_rows/spacing were already @export and already honoured by apply_grid_config, so the only thing a map could say about a field was how densely to sample it - never which field it was, or what the colour meant.
dna.note: field is WHICH RULE the plane obeys. cells is a tiled lattice of saddles - the default is already a field of the third value, repeated; orbit is a centre (closed circles, nothing enters or leaves), sink is a stable node (every trajectory ends at the origin), saddle is the single hyperbolic point the default tiles, shear is parallel layers sliding at different speeds. All four linear fields reuse the stream function's own k=2.5 as their gain, so |v| spans the same range at every value and the colour ramp keeps meaning one thing across the axis. coding is WHAT THE TINT CLAIMS: magnitude is a continuum, direction paints the heading as hue (the optical-flow convention, and the one value where speed is not in the colour at all), banded quantises |v| into four classes (the choropleth claim - a legend where there was a ramp), uniform withholds colour entirely so arrow LENGTH is the only channel left.
dna.kin: field is taken from VectorFieldFlow (vectors.json) and the two values it shares - orbit and sink - name the same phase portrait character for character. It is NOT the same list: spiral and source are absent, and cells, saddle and shear are new. source is absent for a measurement reason, not a taxonomic one - the arrow here is a headless BoxMesh oriented by looking_at, so reversing the sign of the field produces a pixel-identical still under the default coding, and a source would ship as a duplicate frame of sink. coding is taken from cube_lines (primitives.json), where it asks the same question - what does the colour encode - and shares uniform meaning the same withholding. force_field_visualizer, promoted in this same batch, deliberately did NOT take the word field for its four physical laws; that refusal and this reuse are consistent: over there the values are named force laws that fall off differently, here as there they are shapes a synthetic flow is bent into.
dna.still_note: field is the strong axis: cells is a tiled swirl, sink is a starburst, shear is eight parallel rows, and the arrow orientations differ everywhere at once. coding is the thinner measurement - the subject is 96 arrows of 2.5 cm x 18 cm on an otherwise empty plane, so the changed pixels are the arrows only; expect dilution and crop-recheck before believing an INERT verdict on it. direction is the value most likely to bite, since it replaces a two-colour ramp with the full hue circle.

vector_field_grid.name: Vector Field Grid
vector_field_grid.description: Regular grid of arrows over a plane, each pointing along a stream function flow direction. Arrow length and color reflect magnitude.

particle_flow_swarm.name: Particle Flow Swarm
particle_flow_swarm.description: Many small particles ride the same vector field shown in vector_field_grid. Pairs with the grid to demonstrate field effect on bodies.

ftc_bridge.name: FTC Bridge
ftc_bridge.description: An arched bridge labeled with the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. A pulse runs from left pillar (a) to right pillar (b). The change-sequence capstone.

riemann_sum_workbench.name: Riemann Sum Workbench
riemann_sum_workbench.description: An interactive workbench for the midpoint Riemann sum. One slider drives N (rectangle count) through six detents [4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128]; N translucent blue rectangles regenerate under the curve f(x) = ½ + 0.4·sin(2x) + 0.15·cos(5x) on [0, 5]; a live readout shows Σ, the true ∫ ≈ 2.864, and the signed error; a side error-bar shrinks toward green as N grows. The slider IS the limit — at N=4 the polygon visibly under- and overshoots; at N=128 it traces the curve. Paired with the /riemann-sum-gallery web cells of this same instrument frozen at the six N-values.

tangent_slope_workbench.name: Tangent Slope Workbench
tangent_slope_workbench.description: An interactive workbench for the derivative as tangent slope. One slider drives x continuously across [0, 5]; a red marker slides along the curve f(x) = ½ + 0.4·sin(2x) + 0.15·cos(5x); a bright gold tangent line through the marker rotates to match f'(x) = 0.8·cos(2x) − 0.75·sin(5x); a small f'(x) subplot above the main plot tracks the derivative as its own function; a live readout shows f'(x), f(x), an up/down/flat slope word, and x; a side sign indicator arrow tilts up (green) when rising, down (red) when falling, flat (white) at extrema. At local maxima/minima the tangent goes horizontal — the geometric moment of an extremum. Paired with the /tangent-slope-gallery web cells of this same instrument frozen at 8 x-positions. Sibling to riemann_sum_workbench — same f, differentiation vs. integration.

dna.default: tick=fine, evidence=longhand - fine maps to samples=9 and longhand draws the amber curve, the staircase, the secant and its tag, which is the shipped build line for line; the dot radius is now min(0.008, tick_pitch*0.45) and at nine samples the cap is 0.044, so the 0.008 constant is untouched. Zero placements in any map_data.json (the only other file naming this token is its own dressing room), so nothing standing changes either way.
dna.was: samples/span/amp and three colours were @export, but the ONLY route to them was an apply_grid_config that assigned the variable after _ready had already built with 9 and never rebuilt - the knob turned and nothing moved. The artifact ends on 'shrink the frame and the staircase gets finer; it never becomes the curve' and no placement could test the sentence.
dna.note: tick is the halving argument as one ladder, x3 either side of the shipped nine: once=1 (the whole motion as a single frozen frame), coarse=3, fine=9, dense=27, limit=81 - where the eye stops being able to tell and the record is STILL a staircase. It moves the secant too, since the secant is a chord over one frame: at limit it lies visually along the tangent while remaining, by construction, not it. evidence is what the machine puts in the frame for you to check its record against: result = the staircase alone, which looks perfectly correct because there is nothing in shot it could be wrong about; trace = + the true continuous curve; longhand = + the extended secant and its tag. The caption plate is present at every value of both axes, so a measured bite is a bite in the drawing and never in the label.
dna.kin: evidence is the family word (example_1_7 / 1_9 / 2_8 / 2_9, koch_curve, box_counting_dimension, sine_wave_controller), taken character for character. sine_wave_controller is the precedent for a three-value member: there is no fourth thing to withhold here, since the rule is already stated in words on the plate at every value. THE DEFAULT DIFFERS FROM THE FAMILY'S - the motion demos ship as `result` with every exhibit withheld, this one ships with its whole working already on the table - and that is a fact about the artifact, not a drift in the word.
dna.still_note: tick is the strong axis in pixels: once vs limit is 1 step against 81 and changes the picture wholesale. evidence is the sharper claim but the THINNER measurement - the amber curve it withholds is 180 segments at 4 mm on a 1.0 x 0.44 m panel, so expect result-vs-trace to land near the 3% line and crop-recheck before believing an INERT verdict on it.

zeno_staircase.description: The change (calculus) seam. Motion is continuous; the machine reads at frame ticks and holds between (Zeno's arrow, frozen then jump). The amber curve vs the blue staircase; the 'instantaneous' rate it reports is a secant over one frozen frame, not the tangent.
zeno_staircase.name: Zeno Staircase
zeno_staircase.qfep_connection: A station in the bias landscape (doc/SEAM_PER_SEQUENCE.md); the digital-bias seam for change. Bias is conserved; show the seam.
